description: Persistent LCV-XXX backlog. Live source of truth across sessions. The project-manager rehydrates Claude Tasks from this file at session start, and writes back after every status change. PLAN.md, backlog.md, and demand files reflect content but are no longer the live status board. Titles, phases and statuses here are reconciled against the demand-file headers, which are authoritative. Marco 0 (LCV-100..108) shipped; user tags v0.1.0. Marco 1 (LCV-110..119) shipped — functional parity with v1.0.0, targets tag v0.2.0. MARCO 2 (LCV-121..125) IS COMPLETE as of 2026-09-13 - all five Done and reviewed — LCV-121 Done (d584f4d), LCV-122 Done (61d609b, 2a7a9b4, ccaaf6e, ff267ec), LCV-123 Done (6102c68, e7ba0a6, af5ef82). LCV-124 Done (96a8fb4, a1b37aa). LCV-125 Done (8b5fa2c, c6e9d9d), the last demand of the milestone. WHAT MARCO 2 BOUGHT: the agent went from narrating a drawing it could not touch to editing the operator's live document - a whole turn folds into a single Ctrl+Z, a fence stops it dead if the operator draws underneath it, the command line is a keyboard path in, and the panel makes what it did legible. NOBODY TAGS ANYTHING: the user tags v0.1.0 after their own manual smoke run and LCV-089 stays Blocked until they do. TWO NEW DEMANDS opened 2026-09-13 from the LCV-124 review, both Draft, phase 12, neither placed in the drive order yet (project-manager's call): LCV-130 (the suite's network isolation depends on the absence of a proxy - the class of defect that leaks a credential from a green test run) and LCV-131 (typing a full command name such as 'line' pays a model for a CAD word; suggested agent architect, it amends ADR 0003 A2's frozen alias set). LCV-129 is now Ready (refined 4c0b46f) and depends on LCV-125 as well as LCV-123. LCV-132 (Draft, phase 12, opened 1f3cb27) promotes LCV-125's paint-list seam into tests/harness/ and already has a customer in LCV-129 (39a6d6b). THE RELEASE HAZARD IS CLOSED as of LCV-123: panel.rs::submit and its throwaway Document::default() were deleted outright, AGENT_DOCUMENT_EXCEPTIONS in tests/lcv122_source_scans.rs is now [&str; 0] and proven non-vacuous from both directions, and the agent's edits land on the operator's real canvas. Tagging is no longer blocked by that hazard; the banner is deleted from backlog.md. LCV-129 (Draft, phase 12), LCV-127 (Ready, phase 11), LCV-126 (Draft, phase 11) and LCV-128 (Draft, phase 12) are follow-ups outside that drive, in drive order 16 -> 17 -> 18 -> 19 after it. LCV-129 was opened 2026-09-13 and leads them: a hung endpoint has no timeout and no cancel, so it latches agent_busy and repaints forever (LCV-120 through a different door) with no recovery but quitting - the only known defect that can wedge the app in a real user's hands, and the user is about to run their first live prompt against OpenRouter. It is still not part of Marco 2. CI STATUS: GitHub Actions has been DOWN for this repository since ~17:28 UTC 2026-09-13 — every job dies in 2-5 seconds with zero steps recorded, including on a Markdown-only commit pushed deliberately to test it. Read nothing into the red check marks; it is infrastructural (most likely exhausted Actions minutes on a private repo) and is with the team lead as a user-only decision. THE LOCAL GATE IS AUTHORITATIVE for the rest of this milestone: fmt + clippy + cargo test --all --no-fail-fast, run and reported by the reviewer. Last CI-verified demand is LCV-122 (run 34758445630, green on ubuntu-24.04 / windows-2022 / macos-15); LCV-123 and everything after it are local-gate only until Actions comes back.

demands.title: Command-line parser: a pure kernel module for `X,Y`, `@X,Y`, distance, aliases, toggles and zoom
demands.note: ADR 0003 (ac9e796) binds this: module at src/cmdline/, joins the AGENTS.md purity list; ToolKind enum + tools::make() retires BOTH ui/shortcuts.rs::TOOL_KEYS string mapping AND ui/toolbar.rs::make_tool. Refined 36b0056. Product calls: '.' is always the decimal separator and ',' always the coordinate separator, no locale detection; the recall ring is a transcript (duplicates kept, Unknown pushed, Empty not); 'e' maps to Delete and EXTEND gets no alias (v2 binds Key::E to DeleteTool). SHIPPED 66af950; review returned REWORK REQUIRED on one blocking finding and the fix landed as 29ac39a. Reviewer ran six mutation probes and all bit correctly: comma-as-decimal, ring de-dup, e->Extend, a removed ToolKind arm (compile error, no wildcard), and a broken TOOL_KEYS loop (the headless tests/lcv110.rs test caught it, so it is not tautological). The blocking finding was that a blank push left the recall cursor untouched; v1's command-line.ts:192-196 resets historyIndex unconditionally on every Enter, so push() now resets the cursor before the blank-entry early return. 632 -> 661 lib tests. CI green all three platforms (run 34729102013). APPROVED after rework.

demands.title: Wire the parser into the tools: `on_command_input`, R14 prompts, focus-on-typing
demands.note: Biggest demand of Marco 1. ADR 0003 §B fixes on_command_input(ToolInput, &mut Document, &mut History) -> bool; tools never see a string. Prompts use the EXISTING Tool::status_text() pull model (§C); the real gap is CircleTool/ArcTool inheriting name(). Focus: the tool shortcut WINS over command-line focus, so the AC reads 'any alphanumeric that is NOT a bound tool shortcut'. product-owner added anchor() to Move/Circle/Arc but REFUSED it for Rect (ortho would collapse a rect to zero width/height), with a follow-up for architect to split the two meanings of anchor(). RISK: this demand leaves TEXT non-functional until LCV-112 lands, so LCV-112 is not optional. SHIPPED 533e24a + 2f39e9d; review returned REWORK REQUIRED on one blocking finding, fixed in d6a23b7. The finding was spec drift, not a design error: AC 9.4's 'Empty is never pushed' was written in dbf6a7a BEFORE the LCV-110 rework 29ac39a changed CommandHistory::push to reset the recall cursor on a blank entry, so guarding the call site made that already-approved behaviour unreachable in production. Reviewer checked v1 directly and found it does two things on one Enter: command-line.ts:192-196 resets historyIndex unconditionally, while execute() at 76-86 has its own separate blank guard before appending. Reviewer also confirmed the tests/lcv103.rs rename is a legitimate supersession and strictly more discriminating, and that the RECT no-anchor decision rests on a true premise (RectTool::on_pointer_down does discard at or below EPSILON). 661 -> 704 lib tests, 68 -> 86 integration. APPROVED after rework.

demands.title: TEXT complete: raw-input mode for the string, then the height, in exactly one undo step
demands.note: ADR 0003 §D raw-input mode. Height range 0.1..2000 mm, empty means 5.0; out of range keeps the operator's string and re-prompts, never clamps. Exactly one undo entry. Deletes Tool::on_text_input, which LCV-111 is explicitly forbidden from removing. Refined 36b0056. SHIPPED 2ef12af (TextTool rebuilt as Idle -> WaitingText -> WaitingHeight; wants_raw_input()/on_raw_input() added to Tool; on_text_input deleted). Review returned REWORK REQUIRED on one blocking finding, fixed in 307cfad. The finding was a COVERAGE gap, not a wrong behaviour: the re-check of wants_raw_input() AFTER the Enter branch in src/ui/command_line.rs, which releases focus on the same frame a commit returns TEXT to Idle, was correct but untested -- the reviewer reverted the ordering and all 39 lcv103/lcv111/lcv112 tests still passed. Rework added a behavioural test (a bare L the very next frame must activate LINE) and swapped tests/lcv103.rs's enter-double-dispatch vehicle from TextTool to LineTool, since TextTool::on_key lost its Enter arm. Re-review APPROVED: both mutations re-run in a scratch worktree, plus a SURGICAL mutation unguarding only the TOOL_ROUTED_KEYS loop, proving the lcv103 test catches the real defect and not buffer-corruption side effects. LineTool and PolylineTool are the only two tools whose on_key reacts to Enter and each now has an independent witness. 704 -> 718 lib tests, 86 -> 95 integration. CI green all three platforms (run 34733893629). This review also SURFACED LCV-117: the Hershey glyph table renders 22 glyphs below the baseline.

demands.title: Hershey glyph table: 22 alphanumeric glyphs (plus `?`) render below the baseline
demands.note: Defect found during the LCV-112 review, predates it (shipped by LCV-055). src/text/layout.rs places the text origin ON the baseline and maps py = origin.y - hy*scale, so any glyph datum with hy>0 renders BELOW the baseline. 22 of 62 alphanumeric glyphs violate the file's own documented convention (baseline y=0, caps top y=-9, x-height y=-6, descenders y~+4): 0 5 6 8 9 O Q S a b c d e o s t u overshoot with no descender at all, and g j p q y descend to +10/+6/+9/+9/+6 instead of +4. 'O' literally spans y=[-9..9], i.e. a 10mm O is 20mm tall with half below the line. Not a uniform offset -- checked, no affine map repairs 'O' -- so the data is corrupt per-glyph and must be re-authored, not shifted. Survived since LCV-055 because the only cap-height test (layout.rs h_cap_height_matches_height_mm) uses 'H', one of the 40 CORRECT glyphs. Acceptance must be a mechanical whole-table invariant test, not per-glyph eyeballing. Severity comparable to the mirrored-SVG defect D1 closed in Marco 0: it is visible in every exported SVG and in LaserGRBL. Refined bb37da6; product-owner corrected me in four places, notably that my 'no affine transform repairs O' claim was wrong (I missed a third data point) and that my proposed x-height invariant would have failed on seven CORRECT glyphs, since m n r v w x z top at -5 not -6. They also found the real root cause: the bad glyphs, or the bad STROKE inside a good glyph, were authored with the origin at the vertical centre of the body, so a b d p q t y need one stroke moved rather than a redraw and only 0 6 8 O c e o s are true redraws. Scope settled at 23 glyphs (the 22 plus '?'), descenders normalised to exactly +4, 17 punctuation marks exempted by an anti-widening test. SHIPPED d696f7c + c8cebad, 718 -> 729 lib tests, CI green (run 34736564259). Review returned REWORK REQUIRED on one real finding: the AC 14 test scanned EVERY stroke of Q for a lower-right point, but Q's bowl is byte-identical to O's and always supplies one, so the reviewer truncated Q's tail to (1,-3),(4,-3) and the entire suite still passed. The reviewer's second finding, that hershey.rs at 476 lines and layout.rs at 380 breach the 300-line cap, is VOID: ADR 0002 lines 371-375 count implementation lines only and exclude inline #[cfg(test)] blocks, making them 53 and 87. AC 9 was found self-contradictory by implementer and reviewer independently and is being reworded by product-owner; the code already matches the intended reading. Rework 5d48027 scoped the Q assertion to the tail stroke; reviewer re-ran three mutations (truncated tail, deleted tail stroke, Q made byte-identical to O) and all three now fail loudly. Reviewer audited the '.any()' pattern across both test files and confirmed it does not recur. Reviewer RETRACTED the 300-LOC finding. APPROVED. CI green run 34737781075.

demands.title: Confirm discard on New / Open / Exit when the document has unsaved changes
demands.note: Refined 27f2a85. product-owner found that History::revision()/dirty_since is NOT usable as a discard guard: autosave's flush_if_due calls mark_clean() every ~800 ms, so the prompt window would be sub-second. Introduces an independent App::saved_revision written only by mark_saved(). Requires a new src/app/file_ops.rs because src/app/mod.rs is at 293 of the 300 cap. SHIPPED 475d666 (behaviour-neutral relocation of the five action_* wrappers out of src/app/mod.rs, which was at 293/300) + a7df030 (saved_revision / has_unsaved_changes / mark_saved, PendingAction, four request_* guards, poll_close_request with ViewportCommand::CancelClose). 729 -> 746 lib, 95 -> 100 integration. CI green run 34738711513. Review returned REWORK REQUIRED on one finding: AC 3's saved_revision/autosave separation has NO automated guard. The reviewer added 'app.saved_revision = Some(app.history.revision())' inside flush_if_due's due branch -- the exact regression the demand calls existential -- and all 746 tests stayed green. flush_if_due has only one test and it exercises the clean early-return, while the demand's own regression test calls mark_clean() directly rather than flush_if_due. Fix is a source-scan test mirroring file_ops_does_not_import_eframe_or_rfd. Six other mutations all bit. Reviewer also found that inverting has_unsaved_changes fails as a HANG on rfd, not an assertion -> routed to architect, became ADR 0005 and LCV-118. Rework 1cb4ae8 promoted the AC 3 and AC 4 hand-run greps into include_str! source-scan tests (autosave_never_mentions_saved_revision, file_actions_never_calls_mark_clean in src/app/file_ops.rs). Reviewer re-added the saved_revision write inside flush_if_due and exactly one test now fails by name; confirmed the scan reads a sibling file and is not vacuous; git diff a7df030..1cb4ae8 touches only file_ops.rs +38/-0 and ui/dialogs.rs +6/-2. APPROVED. Docs closed 4f96f95.

demands.title: Disarm native file dialogs outside the app binary
demands.note: Opened from the LCV-113 review. ADR 0005 (f44eeb3) decides it. ADR 0002 A4 rule 1 and ADR 0003 F3 trap 1 ban SENDING Ctrl+O/Ctrl+S headless, which is a property of every test SITE; the hazard is a property of product LOGIC. The reviewer inverted has_unsaved_changes and a correctly-written test fell through to the real action_open(), reached rfd and HUNG the test binary -- a CI timeout with no output on all three platforms rather than a named assertion failure. Architect's shape: a private AtomicBool NATIVE_DIALOGS_ARMED in src/io/dialogs.rs with Relaxed ordering, arm_native_dialogs() called as the first statement of crate::run() in src/lib.rs, no disarm, all three wrappers PANIC when disarmed. Panic not None, because None means 'user cancelled' and is a valid return from all three, so an inverted guard would go green down a wrong path. Guard sits at the rfd boundary, NOT on App, so it also covers a test calling crate::io::action_open directly. CRITICAL: a #[cfg(test)] guard CANNOT work -- integration tests link the library as an ordinary dependency with cfg(test) OFF, so the arm would be absent from exactly the binary that hung. The decisive test is a #[should_panic] in tests/ calling the dialog directly. ~40 lines including tests. Does NOT block Marco 1 (no user-visible behaviour, unblocks nothing) but scheduled BEFORE LCV-114, because LCV-114/115 add state that guards upstream of file actions read. SHIPPED fa158c0: static NATIVE_DIALOGS_ARMED AtomicBool in src/io/dialogs.rs, require_armed() first statement of all three wrappers, arm_native_dialogs() re-exported flat from src/io/mod.rs and called first in crate::run(). 748 -> 756 lib, 100 -> 103 integration, CI green 34740729168. Implementer self-caught two self-matching source scans (a !contains("fn disarm") that matched its own sibling test name disarmed_panic_cites_adr_0005, and the literal arm_native_dialogs in tests/lcv118.rs's own module doc comment) and rebuilt both needles with concat!. Review returned REWORK REQUIRED on a THIRD instance of the same bug that neither caught: run_arms_native_dialogs_as_its_first_statement did an unbounded include_str!("lib.rs") whose haystack included the test's own body, so both .find() needles resolved against the test's own source. The reviewer proved all three mandated mutations PASSED, including deleting the arming call outright. Rework 5e74557 bounds the haystack to &src[..cfg_test_at] mirroring guard_is_runtime_not_cfg, and adds a commented-out-line check because pure byte ordering is insensitive to comments; all three mutations now fail by name. CI green 34741796553. Reviewer's remaining finding is structural and NOT actionable: making arm_native_dialogs() a no-op survives the whole gate, because any test that armed the flag would poison the shared AtomicBool for the rest of the binary (ADR 0005 deliberately has no disarm) or fall into a real rfd dialog and hang. Routed to LCV-089's manual smoke checklist instead (4f96f95). APPROVED. Docs closed 4f96f95 and c228edc.

demands.title: Configurable bed size (1..2000 mm), stored in the document and read back on import
demands.note: Refined 27f2a85. Bed size owned by Document::bed_mm (undoable, round-trips); Settings::default_bed_mm seeds File>New and cold boot only; App::bed removed. Default STAYS 400x400 (renamed DEFAULT_BED_*_MM) because re-baselining to v1's 128 would rewrite every LCV-100/LCV-057 golden fixture for zero user gain. flip_y becomes flip_y(y, bed_height_mm). Import precedence width+height > viewBox > 400x400; out-of-range is REJECTED not clamped; opening a file adopts its bed. Implementer updates the AGENTS.md LaserGRBL/SVG checklist. SHIPPED bd49c11 (25 files, +1879/-161). Document::bed_mm owns the bed; flip_y(y, bed_height) takes the axis as a parameter; new src/io/svg/header.rs parses width/height then viewBox then falls back to 400x400; SetBedSize command in src/document/commands/bed.rs; File > Bed size... dialog in src/app/bed_dialog.rs. 756 -> 806 lib, 103 -> 112 integration across 16 binaries, 5 -> 6 doc. CI green 34743397971. APPROVED ON THE FIRST PASS, a milestone first. Reviewer mutated all TEN flip_y call sites to a hardcoded 400 one at a time and every one was caught; stubbing parse_bed to the default failed 13 tests; five further mutations (clamp_bed_mm no-op, SetBedSize::undo no-op, dropped serde(default) on the envelope, Bed::from_size_mm ignoring its argument, OK committing without the unchanged-bed check) all bit. All six bounded source scans were individually shown to discriminate. Implementer disclosed four interpretations, all judged sound: Display rather than {:.4} for the header (AC 5's own wording is self-contradictory and byte-identity forces Display); SetBedSize in commands/bed.rs because commands.rs is a directory; the Settings::save() call kept in the egui half so headless tests cannot write the developer's real config; and validating a present-but-unused width/height/viewBox, which AC 9 already required literally. src/app/mod.rs now measures 296 of the 300 cap: the next App field forces the split ADR 0004 pre-decided.

demands.title: Export preset selector (cut / mark / engrave)
demands.note: Refined 27f2a85. Whole-document export-time preset only; per-entity preset is an explicit Non-goal with a forward pointer. State on App::export_preset, SESSION-ONLY (a sticky preset means yesterday's mark job cuts today's part), always shown as a status-bar label. Depends on LCV-114 for the shared ImportedSvg return type. SHIPPED 2f20fdd (behaviour-neutral: moved impl Default for App + App::new into src/app/init.rs, because mod.rs was at 296/300 and AC 5 adds a field; suite identical across the split) + 24e36aa. 806 -> 825 lib, 112 -> 119 integration across 18 binaries. CI green 34745657869. Byte identity for Preset::Cut verified not just by assertion but by diffing against a real git worktree at c228edc, for a line on the default bed and for line+circle+CCW arc+large CW arc on a 300x180 bed. Every source scan was mutation-verified in both directions, and one positive control ('struct DocumentEnvelope') was found too weak to catch a rename and tightened. Five interpretations disclosed: AC 7's expected-test asserts a pub(crate) fn across the crate boundary, which is unreachable, so the text assertion went to statusbar.rs and the deviation is documented in the test header and the commit message; the demand's U+25B8 glyph differs from the sibling Open Recent U+25B6; bare geometry does NOT lock in Cut, since AC 8 says first group WITH GEOMETRY; the action_new test lives only in the integration file; CHANGELOG left to demand-manager. APPROVED ON THE FIRST PASS. Reviewer reproduced the byte-identity check in real worktrees at c228edc and 422c7e7 rather than trusting the assertion, mutation-tested all six source scans plus five behavioural probes, and none survived. They judged the App-level source-scan substitute for AC 5 and AC 9 honest rather than a false green, since the kernel behaviour is exhaustively tested and only the thin wiring is scanned. Two demand-text defects confirmed for product-owner, both non-blocking: AC 7's expected test asserts a pub(crate) fn across the crate boundary, and AC 8's two sentences genuinely conflict on bare geometry followed by a populated group. Reviewer disclosed that they ran their mutations in the main checkout rather than a worktree, restoring after each and confirming a clean tree; flagged rather than hidden. Docs closed c8370fb.

demands.title: Chrome completion: clickable mode toggles, autosave indicator, F1 shortcuts dialog, Ortho in the View menu
demands.note: Refined 27f2a85. product-owner found View>Zoom in/out ALREADY SHIPPED, so (d) shrank to a regression test plus the one real gap: Ortho/F8 has no checkbox where Grid/F7 and Snap/F3 do. Autosave indicator is three permanent states from a pure format_autosave(), no 'Ns ago' counter and no fade. Also found a latent defect: flush_if_due only runs inside a frame and nothing schedules one, so an idle dirty app may never autosave -> AC 9/10 require request_repaint_after(). CLOSED 2026-09-13 (Done): shipped fd9b4e4 plus 900f0c7, a Windows-only CI fix comparing a path against a forward-slash literal (no production code wrong). CI run 34747953068 green; reviewed APPROVED — the reviewer reproduced both disclosed deviations and found no surviving mutation across 20+ probes. The latent autosave defect this demand predicted was real and was fixed here (schedule_flush_repaint), and LCV-120 later made it load-bearing.

demands.title: Real user paths are injected: `cargo test` stops writing the developer's config and data directories
demands.note: Opened from the LCV-114 review. action_open and action_open_path both end with an unconditional 'let _ = app.settings.save();' (src/io/file_actions.rs:59-91 and :132-156), and Settings::save() (src/io/settings.rs:162) resolves directories::ProjectDirs config_dir()/settings.json with NO test-mode guard. A test calling either would overwrite the DEVELOPER'S OWN ~/.config/lasercad/settings.json, agent_api_key included, with a test Settings::default(). Reviewer confirmed by source reading and deliberately did not execute the path. The hazard PREDATES LCV-114: git show 25e42cc shows both calls already there, dating to LCV-062. LCV-114 inherited it, correctly declined to write the AC 10 test that would have tripped it, and designed its own bed-dialog OK/Cancel split (apply_bed_dialog_result returns bool, draw_bed_dialog does the save) specifically to stay on the safe side of it. Exactly the ADR 0005 problem shape on a different resource, but WORSE to detect: rfd hangs loudly, this writes silently and is only noticed on the next real run. Reviewer's answer to 'does this warrant a follow-up demand' was an explicit yes. Not blocking for LCV-114. Demand file written c8370fb, Draft. architect must be consulted before refinement on whether this extends ADR 0005 or needs its own ADR. CLOSED 2026-09-13 (Done): refined well past the original title — the answer was not a third one-off guard but ADR 0006, real user paths resolved once at boot and injected. Shipped 2d81a14 (implementation), e90c3e0 (rework, reviewer-approved), 0e9c9c4 (doc follow-up). Reviewed APPROVED.

demands.title: The viewport never lets the app idle
demands.note: Opened from the LCV-116 review. src/app/viewport.rs:46 calls ctx.request_repaint() unconditionally under the comment 'Always repaint so cursor-coords and smooth camera motion stay live'. git blame attributes it to 0d1d52b (LCV-105). The reviewer drove the real App::update_ui through egui::Context::run on a clean idle app and measured repaint_delay at 0ns on consecutive frames. Consequence: one CPU core at 100% for the life of every session, a battery defect on a laptop. Second consequence and the reason it surfaced: it silently masks the mechanism LCV-116 AC 9 added. schedule_flush_repaint is correct and tested at its own granularity but is NOT currently what keeps autosave alive; it becomes load-bearing the moment this is fixed, so nobody may delete it as dead code. The design question is what actually needs a live repaint: cursor coordinates and smooth camera motion are both real requirements. architect and product-owner own it. Demand file written c8370fb. CLOSED 2026-09-13 (Done). The one-CPU-core-at-100% claim in this note did NOT reproduce and must not be repeated downstream: the team lead measured 0.0% of a core over 6s idle on Wayland, where the compositor throttles a surface that is not visibly changing. The real defect is that the app ASKS for frames it does not need, which is a genuine cost on any platform that does not throttle, and on battery. Shipped as a private viewport_is_live(response, app) = hovered() || dragged() || !preview_entities.is_empty() guarding the single ctx.request_repaint() in src/app/viewport.rs. The other two repaint sites were already conditional and were not touched: autosave::schedule_flush_repaint (LCV-116, now load-bearing and pinned by tests/lcv120_idle_repaint.rs) and the agent_busy-gated site in src/app/mod.rs. Commits 0e11473 (impl), f118b7c (rework from the blocking review finding), c61f2b5 (Windows-only CI fix in the AC 8 source scan, production code untouched). Reviewed APPROVED, CI green on all three platforms. Follow-up LCV-127 (Ready, phase 11) carries the untested response.dragged() term.

demands.title: The transport speaks tool calls
demands.note: First demand of Marco 2. Shipped 2026-09-13 as a single commit, d584f4d, no rework. New src/agent/wire.rs is the single declaration site for the OpenAI-compatible serde types (ChatMessage / AssistantMessage / ToolCall / ToolCallFunction / Choice / ChatResponse); src/agent/transport.rs now puts a tools array on the wire and parses tool_calls back out, returns wire::AssistantMessage instead of String, and maps HTTP 401 / 429 / 5xx onto distinct human-readable errors with no path that can leak the API key. The hardcoded "gpt-4o" model id and MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_TURN are gone: agent_model and agent_step_budget are real Settings fields (serde defaults per field, so pre-LCV-121 settings.json files still load), the budget defaults to 12 and is clamped to 1..32 at the read site (clamp_step_budget in loop_.rs, per ADR 0007 §D7 — io/settings.rs must not import crate::agent). Reviewed APPROVED with no blocking findings; the reviewer re-ran the gates independently (fmt clean, clippy clean, cargo test --all 893 lib tests / 0 failed / 1 ignored across 26 targets + 6 doc-tests) and ran a 47-mutation pass: 42 killed, 5 survivors, all five judged non-blocking (two equivalent mutants). CI run 34758445630 green on ubuntu-24.04, windows-2022 and macos-15. NO CHANGELOG ENTRY WAS WRITTEN, deliberately: nothing user-visible improved. The new settings have no UI (src/agent/settings_ui.rs still renders only Endpoint URL and API Key — the model and step-budget fields are file-only until LCV-125), and src/agent/panel.rs::submit still dispatches tool calls against a throwaway Document::default(), so between LCV-121 and LCV-123 the agent will confidently report geometry that never reaches the canvas. That is the known, accepted intermediate state recorded in ADR 0007 §'The 121→123 window' and in the release hazard in backlog.md: DO NOT TAG OR CUT A RELEASE until LCV-123 is Done. THREE CARRIED ITEMS, all routed to LCV-123 (where a human first points the transport at a real endpoint) and none of them acted on here: (1) no test anywhere asserts the Authorization header exists — deleting .bearer_auth(api_key) from src/agent/transport.rs:128 leaves the whole suite green; pre-existing since LCV-077, but LCV-121 rewrote all twelve of those tests without closing it. (2) ChatMessage::assistant_with_tool_calls is never called with Some(content) anywhere in src/, so prose a model emits alongside its tool calls is silently dropped from the conversation it reads back. (3) tests/lcv121_source_scans.rs skips comment lines for every scan, so a hardcoded model id reintroduced inside a // comment would survive; behaviourally inert, the real property is pinned elsewhere.

demands.title: The bridge: one action, one command, one undo entry
demands.note: Second of the five Marco 2 demands. DONE 2026-09-13. Shipped as four commits: 61d609b (feat: the document-free bridge, CompositeCommand, History::coalesce_last, TurnFence, src/app/agent_apply.rs), 2a7a9b4 (test, rework from the one blocking review finding: pin the coalescing gate's anchor and the fourth turn exit), ccaaf6e (fix: the lost-answer exit reports the same row as a lost sender - a behaviour change, see below), ff267ec (docs: state agent_poll's turn-exit rule as a property, not a count). Read with 83eb2ff, which amended ADR 0007 §D11 mid-flight from three turn exits to four; the demand cannot be understood without it. WHAT SHIPPED: src/agent/bridge.rs carries the protocol between the worker thread and the UI thread. The worker sends one action at a time with its own one-shot reply sender and blocks; it never holds a Document, a clone, a snapshot or a mutex. The UI thread applies each action through Command + History, so undo, autosave and the dirty flag work with no special case for the agent. A whole agent turn collapses into one undo entry by coalescing after the fact, gated so it can only ever fold the agent's own contiguous entries. History::revision() is a fence: if the user commits something mid-turn the action is refused and the turn ends. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE NOT IN THE DEMAND (ccaaf6e): the fourth turn exit is the reply channel's receiver being gone while the UI thread holds an action - the worker vanished mid-action. It used to end the turn silently; it now writes the same AGENT_LOST_MESSAGE error row as a disconnected channel (src/app/agent_poll.rs). The reviewer raised it as optional and recommended a separate demand; project-manager promoted it to blocking over that recommendation, because a turn that never ends leaves agent_busy latched and src/app/mod.rs requests a repaint every frame while it is set - that is LCV-120 reopening one day after it closed. REVIEW: APPROVED at ff267ec after one rework round. Gates re-run independently by the reviewer - fmt clean, clippy clean, cargo test --all --no-fail-fast 1105 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored across 27 binaries, cargo doc --no-deps back to the 47-warning baseline verified by diffing warning LOCATIONS against 4f6db6d rather than trusting the count. The blocking mutant is now caught by one test, by name, and by no other in the suite; six mutations of the new behaviour all caught. CI green on all three platforms. NO CHANGELOG ENTRY WAS WRITTEN, deliberately - same call as LCV-121 and for the same reason: nothing is operator-visible yet. src/agent/panel.rs::submit still dispatches against a throwaway Document::default(), so the agent's edits stay invisible on canvas until LCV-123, and the CHANGELOG's 'can read and narrate the drawing but does not yet modify it end-to-end from chat' is still accurate. The replacement line is drafted and filed for LCV-123; demand-manager carries it. THE RELEASE HAZARD REMAINS LIVE - LCV-122 did not close it and was never going to (throwaway document is in its own Out of scope). Do not tag until LCV-123 is Done. ONE CORRECTION, do not repeat downstream: the implementer's first report claimed every line added to src/app/mod.rs was test code. Under ADR 0004's awk recipe, which counts implementation LOC only, that file went 265 -> 274. Harmless and well under the cap, but the claim was wrong.

demands.title: The agent turn draws on the operator's real drawing
demands.note: The demand that closes the CHANGELOG's 'reads and narrates but does not modify' sentence, and the one that shuts the release hazard. panel.rs::submit today runs the whole turn against a throwaway Document::default() and drops it when the thread ends; only the final assistant string survives. Worse since LCV-121, because the model can now actually call the tools. DO NOT TAG UNTIL THIS IS DONE. This is also where a human first points the transport at a real endpoint, so it carries the three non-blocking items from the LCV-121 review: (1) no test asserts the Authorization header exists — deleting .bearer_auth(api_key) from transport.rs:128 leaves the suite green (pre-existing since LCV-077); (2) ChatMessage::assistant_with_tool_calls is never called with Some(content), so prose emitted alongside tool calls is dropped from the conversation the model reads back; (3) tests/lcv121_source_scans.rs skips comment lines, so a hardcoded model id inside a // comment would survive (behaviourally inert, the real property is pinned elsewhere). CLOSED 2026-09-13 (Done). SHIPPED AS THREE COMMITS: 6102c68 (feat: run_agent_turn gives up Document and History for an injected ask-callback; panel.rs::submit DELETED; src/app/agent_turn.rs arms the turn and holds the fence and the coalesce gate; agent_poll drains to Empty and clears agent_rx only on a terminal event; query_entities / query_selection; the positional-index contract in the system prompt; the step budget read from Settings and clamped at the read site; the end-of-turn undo-shape note; one transcript row per action), e7ba0a6 (refactor: the rework round that closed BOTH blocking review findings — shallow agent imports through src/agent/mod.rs, and a module header that matches the rule), af5ef82 (docs: src/app/mod.rs's agent_busy repaint guard is pinned by a source scan, not by a timeout). a99978a amended the demand's OWN BODY mid-flight (AC 1 and AC 3, after the code disproved two mutations) and is NOT an implementation commit. REVIEW: APPROVED at af5ef82 after one rework round. VERIFICATION WAS LOCAL, NOT CI — do not repeat a CI-green claim for this demand. GitHub Actions has been down for this repository since ~17:28 UTC 2026-09-13 (every job dies in 2-5s with zero steps, including on a Markdown-only commit pushed to test it), so the red checks on these commits carry no information about the code. At af5ef82 the reviewer independently ran cargo fmt --all -- --check clean, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings clean, and cargo test --all --no-fail-fast 1153 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored across 28 binaries. THE RELEASE HAZARD IS CLOSED. panel.rs::submit — the function that dispatched tool calls against a throwaway Document::default() — was deleted outright rather than adapted; the panel now renders and reports (116 implementation LOC). AGENT_DOCUMENT_EXCEPTIONS in tests/lcv122_source_scans.rs is now [&str; 0], and the reviewer proved it is not vacuous from both directions: reintroducing document state into src/agent/panel.rs failed the scan, and then re-opening the exception list to smuggle it past failed again on a second, independent assertion. The hazard banner is deleted from backlog.md. CHANGELOG ENTRY WRITTEN — the first of Marco 2 to reach the changelog (LCV-121 and LCV-122 both shipped with none, deliberately, because nothing was operator-visible yet). The stale sentence 'The agent can read and narrate the drawing but does not yet modify it end-to-end from chat' was REPLACED IN PLACE inside the existing agent-harness bullet, whose reference now reads LCV-076..LCV-080, LCV-121, LCV-122, LCV-123. Two accuracy points baked into the wording: the single-Ctrl+Z fold holds only for an UNINTERRUPTED turn (a mid-turn user edit trips the fence, ends the turn, and leaves what was already applied as separate undo entries — src/app/agent_poll.rs::undo_note says exactly that to the operator), and a query in the middle of a turn does not break the fold. FOLLOW-UP OPENED FROM THIS REVIEW: LCV-129 (Draft, phase 12, drive order 16) — the transport still has no timeout and the panel no cancel, which is the one way a turn can still latch agent_busy. Doc close-out commit 73effdb.

demands.title: The command line can reach the agent
demands.note: Parallelizable with LCV-125 once LCV-123 is Done. Keyboard-first routing: ':' and '/ai' from the command line reach the agent, so the operator never has to leave the keyboard for the mouse-only side panel. src/agent/classifier.rs is named in PLAN.md's module tree and in ADR 0007 §D8's file table and does not exist yet; the routing decision belongs where app/cmdline.rs::submit currently produces CommandInput::Unknown. PLAN.md's LCV-080 row has always claimed this behaviour. CLOSED 2026-09-13 (Done). SHIPPED AS TWO COMMITS: 96a8fb4 (feat: the pure src/agent/classifier.rs with Route::{Cad, Agent, Unavailable}, and the ADR 0007 D9 precedence wired into src/app/cmdline.rs::submit behind the existing raw-input early return, so ':' and '/ai' always send, CAD input always stays CAD, and an Unknown line reaches the model only when a key is configured), a1b37aa (fix: the rework that closed the one blocking finding). a0131ef corrected AC 2's 'z' row and recorded the CAD-word hazard - a body amendment by product-owner, NOT an implementation commit. REVIEW: APPROVED at a1b37aa. THE BLOCKING FINDING IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING THIS MILESTONE FOUND AND IT IS NOT ABOUT THE COMMAND LINE. The tests pointed at http://127.0.0.1:1 on the assumption that a closed loopback port cannot be reached. IT CAN. reqwest::blocking::Client::new() sets auto_sys_proxy: true and reqwest 0.12 has NO loopback bypass, so with HTTP_PROXY set - normal on a corporate network or a self-hosted runner - the closed port is never dialled and the request is handed to the proxy. The reviewer stood up a capturing listener and recorded real POSTs leaving the machine carrying 'authorization: Bearer sk-test-DO-NOT-LEAK', the entire system prompt and the operator's prompt text, WHILE THE SUITE REPORTED 11 PASSED / 0 FAILED THROUGHOUT. A green suite that exfiltrates a credential is the worst shape a test can take. THE FIX makes the endpoint UNPARSEABLE rather than unreachable, so send() fails in Url::parse before a socket exists and before any proxy is consulted; the_test_endpoint_cannot_reach_a_proxy pins it with the old loopback spelling as its control. Re-run with four proxy variables set: 12 passed, zero captured requests, zero connect() syscalls. The transport was deliberately NOT given .no_proxy() - that would break real operators behind a corporate proxy to buy a test convenience. What the fix did not reach is the rest of the suite: that is LCV-130. VERIFICATION WAS LOCAL, NOT CI - do not repeat a CI-green claim. At a1b37aa the reviewer independently ran fmt clean, clippy clean under -D warnings, and cargo test --all --no-fail-fast 1184 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored across 29 binaries, after cargo clean -p lasercad rather than trusting the implementer's numbers. 1184 IS THE CORRECTED FIGURE; earlier briefs said 1183. LCV-122 is still the last CI-verified demand. KNOWN HAZARD SHIPPED BY DESIGN, NOT A DEFECT OF THIS DEMAND: with a key configured, a line the CAD grammar does not recognise is a PAID round trip. The demand accepts that for typos like 'lien', but product-owner then found the grammar accepts only the single-letter aliases plus 'text', so 'line', 'circle' and every other full AutoCAD command name is unrecognised and reaches the model. That is LCV-131. LCV-124 shipped exactly the precedence its AC 2 and ADR 0007 D9 specify. CHANGELOG ENTRY WRITTEN, worded so it cannot be read as 'typing line draws a line locally', and keeping the load-bearing sentence that text typed into a TEXT entity is never sent - if the classifier were ever called before the raw-input check, an operator's TEXT string would be posted to a language model. Doc close-out commit ac295e6.

demands.title: The panel shows what the agent did to the drawing
demands.note: Parallelizable with LCV-124 once LCV-123 is Done. Two gaps: (a) the transcript is unreadable — panel.rs renders four role values and drops everything else into a grey ui.label, which is where ADR 0007 §D5's index-shift disclosure and the end-of-turn undo-shape note currently land; if the operator cannot pick those out of the column the disclosure does not exist. (b) The two settings LCV-121 added are unreachable: Settings::agent_model and Settings::agent_step_budget are honoured, but settings_ui.rs still draws only Endpoint URL and API Key. This demand is the ONLY reason it is honest to describe those settings as user-facing, which is why LCV-121 shipped with no CHANGELOG entry. CLOSED 2026-09-13 (Done). THE LAST DEMAND OF MARCO 2; IT CLOSES THE MILESTONE. Shipped as two commits: 8b5fa2c (feat: the six transcript roles plus the fallback arm in src/agent/panel.rs, the ADR 0007 D5 index-shift disclosure and the end-of-turn undo-shape note made findable rather than buried in grey prose, and src/agent/settings_ui.rs grown to reach the model name and the per-turn step budget with an always-visible plaintext-key warning), c6e9d9d (the rework). 269ff1f was a body amendment by product-owner - absorbed the settings_ui deep-path fix and corrected the LOC numbers - NOT an implementation commit. REVIEW: APPROVED at c6e9d9d after one rework round. ONE CORRECTION TO THE HANDOFF, do not repeat 'no source file changed in the rework': c6e9d9d does touch src/agent/settings_ui.rs, but only INSIDE its own #[cfg(test)] mod tests block, re-anchoring the AC 9 scan on RichText::new(STEP_BUDGET_HELP) instead of on the constant's name, which the const declaration alone already satisfied. No IMPLEMENTATION line changed. The implementation was correct on every acceptance criterion from 8b5fa2c; the blocking finding was that the tests were blind to it. WHY THAT FINDING OUTLIVES THE DEMAND: every scan asserted that a call was WRITTEN; nothing asserted that the PAINT HAPPENED. Five mutants survived fmt, clippy -D warnings and all 1208 tests - wrapping the render loop so every transcript row collapsed into one paragraph; iterating .rev() so the transcript read newest-first; skipping the note arm so the undo-shape note never reached the screen; and hiding the plaintext-key warning and the step-budget explanation on exactly the frame an operator is about to paste a key into. Each breaks a stated AC and each was invisible. egui 0.29.1 cannot be asked for a pixel, but Context::run returns the paint list and every Shape::Text carries the exact string and the position it was laid out at. The reviewer's verdict is that the rework is STRONGER THAN THE FIX THEY SPECIFIED: it recurses into Shape::Vec, which their own version missed; it adds an assertion nobody asked for, proving that with a key set the key is painted nowhere and the masked row shares no character with it; and it scopes by clip-rect containment rather than by y, because one frame paints five interleaving surfaces. They re-planted all six original mutants plus five fresh ones and killed all eleven, confirmed the 26 existing scans survived with exactly two added and none removed, and ran the paint tests 50 consecutive times with zero failures. That seam is now LCV-132. VERIFICATION WAS LOCAL, NOT CI: at c6e9d9d fmt clean, clippy clean, cargo test --all --no-fail-fast 1208 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored across 30 binaries. LCV-122 REMAINS THE LAST CI-VERIFIED DEMAND IN THIS PROJECT and the record should keep saying so. CHANGELOG ENTRY WRITTEN in operator terms: the labelled transcript rows, the undo-shape note, the findable renumbering sentence, the model and step-budget fields reachable without hand-editing settings.json, and the always-visible plaintext-key warning. Doc close-out commit 6e1d142.

demands.title: The drag term of `viewport_is_live` has no behavioural test
demands.note: Opened from the LCV-120 review and unblocked by it (LCV-120 Done: 0e11473, f118b7c, c61f2b5). viewport_is_live = hovered() || dragged() || !preview_entities.is_empty(); the hovered and preview terms each have a behavioural witness with a negative control in tests/lcv120_idle_repaint.rs, but dragged() has none — only a source scan proving the text is present, which says nothing about what happens when the operator pans. Not academic: dragged() is what keeps the camera moving while the middle button is held, so if it regresses a pan stutters or freezes mid-stroke. Phase 11, not part of the Marco 2 drive.

demands.title: `AGENTS.md`'s normative per-file and per-symbol enumerations have no scan
demands.note: Draft, opened by demand-manager 2026-09-13 and WIDENED the same day on the reviewer's recommendation; NEXT AGENT IS product-owner, who writes Scope / Out of scope / Acceptance criteria / Expected tests. Status stays Draft and it is NOT scheduled ahead of Marco 2. THE CLASS OF BUG: AGENTS.md carries enumerations that are normative PER ENTRY - each name in the list carries a rule for that name, and in several cases the list is the only statement of the invariant. Nothing enforces any of them, and a name missing from a list is a name with no stated rule. TWO KNOWN INSTANCES, one demand. (1) The src/agent/ purity buckets in AGENTS.md section Purity rule: egui-allowed (panel.rs, settings_ui.rs) vs kernel-pure (classifier.rs, wire.rs, transport.rs, tools.rs, bridge.rs, loop_.rs). A new file under src/agent/ can appear in neither and nothing fails; bridge.rs landed with LCV-122 and sat unclassified until a human noticed. (2) The agent_busy / agent_rx single-writer claim in AGENTS.md section Event flow -> Repaint policy: agent_busy set in exactly one place (src/agent/panel.rs::submit), cleared in exactly one (src/app/agent_poll.rs::end_turn). That sentence is what makes the 'if self.agent_busy' repaint guard a guard rather than a latch, i.e. the argument that LCV-120 stays closed. The LCV-122 reviewer planted app.agent_busy = false; and app.agent_rx = None; in src/agent/panel.rs and BOTH SURVIVED THE WHOLE SUITE. The neighbouring repaint claim in the same paragraph IS scanned (every_repaint_request_in_src_is_conditional in src/app/viewport.rs); the busy-flag half is the only unscanned sentence left in it. ONE DEMAND, NOT TWO: both scans share one file and most of one mechanism - opening LCV-129 was considered and rejected on that ground. REVIEWER'S SKETCH FOR SCAN B, kept in the body: assert concat!("agent_busy", " = false") appears in exactly one file under src/ and that file is agent_poll.rs; same for concat!("agent_rx", " = None") allowing init.rs as the one startup exception; positive control that agent_busy = true appears in exactly one file and that file is panel.rs. The needle must be the CLEAR, not any assignment: agent_rx = Some(..) legally has two writers today (panel.rs::submit arms it, agent_poll.rs puts the receiver back on TryRecvError::Empty). tests/lcv122_source_scans.rs already has every piece of machinery for both scans - rs_files, implementation_or_all, files_containing, the comment-line skip and the concat! discipline. CONSTRAINTS THAT MUST SURVIVE REFINEMENT: (a) scan A is ONE-DIRECTIONAL ONLY - fail when a file exists and is unlisted, never when the list names a file that does not exist yet, because the list already names classifier.rs which LCV-124 has not created and that forward commitment is a feature; (b) the two known traps, now applying to both scans - the self-matching include_str! scan (wrong six times in this repo; bound the haystack at the bare #[cfg(test)] at column 0 and build needles with concat!, canonical example guard_is_runtime_not_cfg at src/io/dialogs.rs:179) and the path separator (rebuild paths from components() joined with /, never display() or to_string_lossy(), which broke CI in LCV-116 and LCV-120). OPEN QUESTION STILL OPEN FOR product-owner: src/agent/mod.rs is named in NEITHER bucket today, so scan A as described fails on main on first run - refinement must decide exempt-by-name vs add-to-kernel-pure, and say so in AGENTS.md either way. OUT OF SCOPE AND NOT REOPENED: the AGENTS.md module tree, which the architect declared explicitly non-exhaustive on 2026-09-13 - it is orientation, so a gap there is cosmetic. The demand FILE NAME still reads agent-purity-list-has-no-scan and was left alone deliberately so links keep resolving; the title is the scope. No dependencies, but NOT part of Marco 2: do not drive ahead of LCV-123, LCV-124 or LCV-125. Phase 12, drive order 19 (was 18; LCV-129 was opened 2026-09-13 and takes the lead of the post-Marco-2 follow-up drive).

demands.title: A hung endpoint wedges the app: the agent turn has no timeout and no cancel
demands.note: Draft, opened by demand-manager 2026-09-13 from the LCV-123 review; NEXT AGENT IS product-owner, who writes Scope / Out of scope / Acceptance criteria / Expected tests and decides the timeout duration. THE DEFECT: src/agent/transport.rs:127 builds reqwest::blocking::Client::new() with NO .timeout(..), and reqwest's default is unbounded. CONSEQUENCE CHAIN, which is why this is a demand and not a footnote: a hung endpoint blocks the worker thread forever -> the worker never sends a terminal event -> agent_poll::end_turn is never reached -> agent_busy never clears -> src/app/mod.rs requests a repaint every frame while agent_busy is set, for the rest of the session. That is LCV-120 REOPENING THROUGH A DIFFERENT DOOR, two days after LCV-120 closed, and it is exactly the latch ADR 0007 section D11 warns about. There is also no cancel affordance anywhere in the agent panel, so the operator's only recovery is to quit the app, losing unsaved work unless autosave happened to fire. PRE-EXISTING: true since the transport was written in LCV-077, NOT a regression from LCV-123 - but LCV-123 is the commit that puts a real operator in front of a real endpoint for the first time, which turns a latent defect into a reachable one. TWO PARTS AND BOTH ARE NEEDED. (1) A client timeout, so the worker eventually gives up and sends a terminal event and the turn ends through the normal path. DO NOT LET REFINEMENT INVENT A NEW EXIT: ADR 0007 section D11 enumerates exactly four turn exits and every one of them goes through agent_poll::end_turn, the only place in the program that writes agent_busy = false or clears agent_rx; a timeout must surface as an EXISTING terminal event, not a fifth exit. Duration is refinement's call - long enough for a slow model to think, short enough that a human does not assume a crash. (2) A Cancel affordance in the agent panel that ends the turn through end_turn; the reviewer's sketch is to drop agent_rx. THE SHARP EDGE, which refinement must not gloss: the worker thread blocks on a rendezvous reply channel (ADR 0007 D2/D3), so cancelling from the UI side has to leave the worker able to notice and unwind rather than blocking forever on a send nobody will answer - D11 arm (4) is the mirror case and the two halves should be reasoned about together. That interaction is the genuinely hard part of this demand. WHY NOT JUST A TIMEOUT: the timeout alone leaves the operator staring at a spinner for the whole timeout window with no way out; the cancel alone leaves a truly wedged connection hanging. Both, or the defect is only half closed. ROOM FOR THE BUTTON: src/agent/panel.rs is 116 implementation LOC after LCV-123 stripped submit out of it, src/agent/transport.rs is 156 - neither is near the 300 cap. demands.title: The test suite's isolation from the network depends on the absence of a proxy
demands.note: Draft, opened 2026-09-13 from the LCV-124 review; body written by product-owner at 348fd0c, 303a3d1, dbad29f and still being edited at the time of registration. NEXT AGENT IS product-owner to declare refinement finished, then implementer-rust. THE DEFECT: the test suite's isolation from the network holds only while no proxy is configured. reqwest::blocking::Client::new() enables system-proxy discovery and reqwest 0.12 has no loopback bypass, so a fixture pointing at a closed loopback port is dialled THROUGH THE PROXY instead of failing locally. The LCV-124 reviewer proved it with a capturing listener: real POSTs left the machine carrying the bearer token, the system prompt and the operator's prompt text while the suite reported 11 passed / 0 failed. LCV-124 fixed ITS OWN fixture at a1b37aa by making the endpoint unparseable rather than unreachable; what that did not reach is the rest of the suite, which is this demand. NOT REOPENED AS PART OF LCV-124: git diff 96a8fb4~1 HEAD -- src/agent/transport.rs is empty, so LCV-124 never opened that file, and holding it open for a defect in a file it never touched would land an unreviewed fix against acceptance criteria that say nothing about it - confirmed independently by reviewer-rust. THE SEVERITY SPLIT THE BODY RECORDS: under a capturing proxy at HEAD, the mockito-bound tests send 24 requests and 23 of them FAIL (loud, announces itself), while unreachable_endpoint_is_a_request_error sends 1 request and PASSES (silent - it leaks and stays green). The silent one is the demand's ordering argument. DO NOT ANSWER THIS WITH .no_proxy() ON THE TRANSPORT: that breaks real operators behind a corporate proxy to buy a test convenience, and LCV-124 declined it deliberately. A manual proxy run has also been added as the ninth step of LCV-089's manual smoke checklist (9768f7e), so the hazard is covered before any tag even if this demand has not shipped. This is the class of defect that leaks a credential from a green test run; project-manager owns where it lands in the drive order.

demands.title: Typing `LINE` sends the word "line" to a language model
demands.note: Draft, opened 2026-09-13 from the LCV-124 review; body written by product-owner at 0c24170. SUGGESTED AGENT IS architect, NOT an implementer, because part of it amends ADR 0003 A2's FROZEN alias set; architect then hands to implementer-rust. THE DEFECT: with an API key configured, a line the CAD grammar does not recognise is routed to the model - a PAID round trip. LCV-124 accepted that for typos like 'lien', which is the behaviour its AC 2 and ADR 0007 D9 specify and is NOT a defect of LCV-124. What product-owner then found is the size of the hole: the grammar accepts only the SINGLE-LETTER tool aliases plus 'text', so 'line', 'circle' and every other full AutoCAD command name is unrecognised and goes to the model instead of drawing. An operator typing the command names they know from R14 pays a model for them. The CHANGELOG entry for LCV-124 is worded so it cannot be read as 'typing line draws a line locally'; when this ships, that caveat comes back out.
